CALIFORNIA PREGNANCY DISABILITY LEAVE LAW (GOV. CODE § 12945) — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's pregnancy disability leave law, Government Code Section 12945, part of the Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA). Section 12945 is a separate statute from the California Family Rights Act (CFRA), Government Code Section 12945.2, and from the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) — it addresses leave for an employee disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition, on its own track from CFRA/FMLA family-care and bonding leave. Where a specific employer and employee are named below, those names are Acme, Inc. and Jordan Lee; this sheet can also be read on its own, without any specific employer or employee named, as a general reference to what this statute says. This sheet states the law; it does not evaluate any particular leave request or employer policy, and it is not a substitute for individualized legal advice.

THE CORE LEAVE ENTITLEMENT
Government Code Section 12945 makes it an unlawful employment practice for a covered employer to refuse to allow an employee disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition to take a leave for a reasonable period of time not to exceed four months, and thereafter to refuse to allow the employee to return to work, as set forth in the applicable regulations. 'Reasonable period of time' is defined by the statute as the period during which the employee is actually disabled on account of pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition — not a fixed calendar entitlement that every employee receives regardless of their own disability duration. During that leave, the employee is entitled to utilize any accrued vacation leave. An employer may require an employee who plans to take this leave to give the employer reasonable notice of the date the leave will commence and its estimated duration.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "For an employer to refuse to allow an employee disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition to take a leave for a reasonable period of time not to exceed four months and thereafter return to work, as set forth in the council’s regulations."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945(a)(1) (leginfo text), California Government Code, pregnancy disability leave, core entitlement and duration (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.)
  "Reasonable period of time means that period during which the employee is disabled on account of pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945(a)(1) (leginfo text), California Government Code, pregnancy disability leave, 'reasonable period of time' defined (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.)
  "The employee shall be entitled to utilize any accrued vacation leave during this period of time."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945(a)(1) (leginfo text), California Government Code, pregnancy disability leave, use of accrued vacation (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.)
  "An employer may require an employee who plans to take a leave pursuant to this subdivision to give the employer reasonable notice of the date the leave shall commence and the estimated duration of the leave."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945(a)(1) (leginfo text), California Government Code, pregnancy disability leave, employer notice requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.)
  Known gap: The four-month figure is a statutory cap on the outer length of leave tied to actual disability, not a guaranteed four months regardless of medical need — an employee disabled for a shorter period is entitled to leave for that shorter period, and the statute does not entitle an employee to leave beyond four months under this section. The statute delegates the specific mechanics of what 'thereafter return to work' requires — including whether an employee returns to the same or a comparable position — to regulations adopted by the responsible council; this document quotes only the statute's own text from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and does not independently verify the content of those regulations. This clause also does not cover Section 12945(a)(3), a separate reasonable-accommodation and temporary-transfer right for pregnancy-related conditions embedded in the same statute, which this document doesn't address.

COVERED EMPLOYERS
Section 12945 does not state its own employee-count threshold; instead, its opening subdivision places it 'in addition to' the provisions governing pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition found elsewhere in this part, including Section 12926 — the definitions section for the part of the Government Code that includes Section 12945. Section 12926 defines 'employer,' for these purposes, as any person regularly employing five or more persons, or acting as an agent of such an employer, and separately as the state and any political or civil subdivision of the state and cities, but excludes a religious association or corporation not organized for private profit.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "In addition to the provisions that govern pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition in Sections 12926 and 12940, each of the following shall be an unlawful employment practice, unless based upon a bona fide occupational qualification:"
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945(a) (leginfo text), California Government Code, pregnancy disability leave, cross-reference to definitions (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.)
  "“Employer” includes any person regularly employing five or more persons, or any person acting as an agent of an employer, directly or indirectly, the state or any political or civil subdivision of the state, and cities, except as follows:"
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12926(d) (leginfo text), California Government Code, FEHA definitions, 'employer' definition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12926.)
  "“Employer” does not include a religious association or corporation not organized for private profit."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12926(d) (leginfo text), California Government Code, FEHA definitions, religious-nonprofit exclusion (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12926.)
  Known gap: Section 12945 itself is silent on employer size; this clause's coverage conclusion rests on Section 12926's general 'employer' definition, which Section 12945(a) expressly cross-references as one of the provisions it supplements. This document doesn't independently verify how 'regularly employing five or more persons' is counted for a business with multiple related entities, franchises, or a staffing-agency arrangement, and doesn't address the separate religious-nonprofit exclusion beyond quoting it.

GROUP HEALTH PLAN COVERAGE DURING LEAVE
It is also an unlawful employment practice for a covered employer to refuse to maintain and pay for group health plan coverage for an eligible employee who takes leave under Section 12945, for the duration of the leave, not to exceed four months over the course of a 12-month period commencing on the date the leave begins, at the level and under the conditions that would have applied had the employee continued working. An employer is not barred from voluntarily maintaining and paying for that coverage beyond four months.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "For an employer to refuse to maintain and pay for coverage for an eligible employee who takes leave pursuant to paragraph (1) under a group health plan, as defined in Section 5000(b)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, for the duration of the leave, not to exceed four months over the course of a 12-month period, commencing on the date the leave taken under paragraph (1) begins, at the level and under the conditions that coverage would have been provided if the employee had continued in employment continuously for the duration of the leave."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945(a)(2)(A) (leginfo text), California Government Code, pregnancy disability leave, group health plan coverage during leave (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.)
  "Nothing in this paragraph shall preclude an employer from maintaining and paying for coverage under a group health plan beyond four months."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945(a)(2)(A) (leginfo text), California Government Code, pregnancy disability leave, coverage beyond four months permitted (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.)
  Known gap: The statute separately allows an employer to recover the premiums it paid to maintain coverage if the employee fails to return from leave after the leave period has expired, for a reason other than taking further leave under the California Family Rights Act or a continuing, recurring, or new qualifying health condition or other circumstance beyond the employee's control — this document does not restate that recovery mechanism's full text or the separate rule for state-agency employers governed by collective bargaining agreements.

HOW THIS LEAVE RELATES TO CFRA AND FMLA
The California Family Rights Act (CFRA) statute, Government Code Section 12945.2, states that it 'shall be construed as separate and distinct from Section 12945' — the pregnancy disability leave law described in this sheet. CFRA's own list of qualifying reasons separately excludes leave for 'disability on account of pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions' from the employee's-own-serious-health-condition category that would otherwise trigger CFRA leave. Consistent with that separation, Section 12945.2 states that an employee is entitled to take, in addition to the leave provided under CFRA and the federal FMLA, the leave provided for in Section 12945, if the employee is otherwise qualified for that leave.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "This section shall be construed as separate and distinct from Section 12945."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.2(n) (leginfo text), California Government Code, California Family Rights Act, separateness from pregnancy disability leave law (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.2.)
  "Leave because of an employee’s own serious health condition that makes the employee unable to perform the functions of the position of that employee, except for leave taken for disability on account of pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.2(b)(5)(C) (leginfo text), California Government Code, California Family Rights Act, pregnancy-disability exclusion from CFRA's own-condition category (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.2.)
  "An employee is entitled to take, in addition to the leave provided for under this section and the FMLA, the leave provided for in Section 12945, if the employee is otherwise qualified for that leave."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945.2(p) (leginfo text), California Government Code, California Family Rights Act, additive entitlement to Section 12945 leave (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.2.)
  Known gap: This document does not independently verify the FMLA's own statutory or regulatory text on how federal FMLA leave interacts with California's Section 12945 leave; it states only what the California statutes say about the relationship. This document also does not resolve, for any individual's specific circumstances, whether or how much of a given absence would be treated as Section 12945 leave, CFRA leave, or FMLA leave in combination — that determination depends on facts and application of these several statutes together. The CFRA document in this corpus (Government Code Section 12945.2) covers CFRA's own eligibility, family-care and medical-leave categories, restoration rights, and its own relationship to FMLA in more detail, and is not duplicated here.

NO INTERFERENCE, AND RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER PREGNANCY-DISCRIMINATION PROTECTIONS
It is also an unlawful employment practice for a covered employer to interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise of, or the attempt to exercise, any right provided under Section 12945. Section 12945 itself states that it is not to be construed to affect any other provision of law relating to sex discrimination or pregnancy, or to diminish the coverage of pregnancy, childbirth, or a related medical condition under any other provision of the same part, including Section 12940(a).

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "For an employer to interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise of, or the attempt to exercise, any right provided under this section."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945(a)(4) (leginfo text), California Government Code, pregnancy disability leave, prohibited interference (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.)
  "This section shall not be construed to affect any other provision of law relating to sex discrimination or pregnancy, or in any way to diminish the coverage of pregnancy, childbirth, or a medical condition related to pregnancy or childbirth under any other provision of this part, including subdivision (a) of Section 12940."
  — Cal. Gov. Code § 12945(b) (leginfo text), California Government Code, pregnancy disability leave, non-diminishment of other pregnancy-discrimination coverage (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=12945.)
  Known gap: This document does not independently verify what Section 12940(a) or other provisions of this part separately provide beyond quoting Section 12945's own reference to them. All citations for this clause are subdivisions of the same statute, Government Code Section 12945 — different parts of one section, not independent sources confirming each other.

LEAVE REQUEST
Jordan Lee requests leave under Government Code Section 12945 as described below.

Disabling condition (pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical condition): _______________________________________________
Requested start date: _______________
Estimated duration of leave: _______________
Expected return-to-work date: _______________
Accrued vacation leave to be used during this period, if any: _______________________________________________

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Please sign below to acknowledge this leave request and the terms above.

Employee: Jordan Lee
Date: _______________

—
